_what: The shape OpenCode itself writes for an assistant message, so the converter can be checked against OpenCode instead of against our own assumptions.
_why: tests/test_session_history.py builds its OpenCode database with a hand-written CREATE TABLE that mirrors what our writer uses. That can only ever confirm the writer agrees with itself: when the transcript loaded fine but the first prompt died on a field OpenCode needed and we never wrote (modelID/providerID), every test stayed green. Keys derived from real rows fail instead.

_derived_from.note: 'required' are the keys present in every one of those messages; 'situational' appeared in some (error on aborted turns, finish on completed ones, summary/variant occasionally).

_refresh: Re-derive against a real ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db after an OpenCode upgrade: select assistant messages from sessions whose version is not '1.0.0' (ours), intersect their key sets for 'required', union-minus-intersection for 'situational'. A stale fixture is visible and fixable; an assumption baked into a test is neither.
